summary: High P95 tail latency after enabling new quantization profile + KV prefetch — request assisted safe-toggle checklist
description:
Issue summary:
Customer deployed two optimizer changes in prod earlier today: a new quantization profile (profile id qp-2026-03-13-v3) and enabled kv_prefetch=true at the serving-group level. Within ~30 minutes they observed a sharp increase in P95 token latency from ~120ms to ~620ms and intermittent request timeouts for long streaming requests. The issue impacts multiple routes and is causing user-facing latency spikes for LexiHealth's triage assistant flows.

Impact:
- Increased P95 token latency across affected model variants.
- Streaming sessions hitting websocket disconnects after 10–20s in ~5% of requests.
- Business impact: slowdown of patient triage flows; customer marked as Priority-1.

Environment:
- Redwood Dedicated pool: rwd-dedicated-lexi-01 (prod us-east)
- Serving groups: sg-lexi-triage-a, sg-lexi-triage-b
- Model variants: redwood-open-7b-quant-8bit (pinned), gptx-13b-qat (fallback)

Recent changes (per customer):
1) Applied quant profile: qp-2026-03-13-v3 via Console rollout at 2026-03-13T13:22:00Z.
2) Enabled kv_prefetch=true on both serving groups at 2026-03-13T13:47:00Z.

Steps to reproduce (customer):
1) Send long-context streaming prompt (~1.5k tokens) to route /v1/generate/triage with concurrency 8.
2) Observe slow first-token times in traces and increased P95 across the Service Route dashboard.

Observed behavior:
- P50 stable, P95 and P99 jumped significantly after changes.
- Kernel-level slowdowns seen in runtime metrics: token processing time per-step increased.
- KV prefetch metrics show spike in disk IO wait and prefetch read latencies.

Expected behavior:
- No material change in P95 after applying quant/kv adjustments; throughput should be preserved or improved.

Attachments:
- Snippets of service traces and perf histograms provided by customer (attached in ticket).
- Sample logs: "kernel: op_conv_slow_path: avg 3.2ms -> 8.9ms", "kv_prefetch: read_latency_ms p95 145 -> 980".

Immediate mitigation attempted by customer:
- Rolled forward traffic to fallback variant (gptx-13b-qat) with partial success but still high P95 on that variant.
- Reduced concurrency on client side to 4 which reduced error rate but not P95.

Customer request:
- Assistance with a safe sequence to toggle/undo the optimizer changes with minimal customer downtime and guidance on verification before and after each step.
investigation:
Summary of findings:
1) Timeline correlation: quant profile rollout preceded KV prefetch enable. Both changes overlap with latency spike.
2) Kernel compatibility: qp-2026-03-13-v3 appears to select an experimental GEMM kernel for certain sequence lengths. That kernel has higher per-token latency at 2048+ context in this runtime build.
3) KV prefetch interaction: kv_prefetch=true causes aggressive upstream block prefetch which increases IO contention on node-local SSDs for this workload pattern (many long contexts, high KV hit rate).
4) Autoscaling and cgroup traces show GPU utilization remained below capacity; CPU and IO were saturated during spikes.
Hypothesis: The quant profile selection resulted in higher per-step CPU overhead for kernel marshalling on long sequences; combined with aggressive KV prefetch this pushed the host IO/CPU path into queuing, increasing token P95 and causing stream disconnects.
Evidence: correlated timestamps across Console rollout audit, runtime logs, and node metrics (attached links).
Suggested priority sequence (safe): see resolution field for step-by-step commands and verification checks.

resolution:
Workaround / rollback checklist (executed as of 2026-03-13T17:10Z for sg-lexi-triage-a, sg-lexi-triage-b):
1) Controlled disable of kv_prefetch (canary then global):
   - Command (canary on group B): redwoodctl serving-group update sg-lexi-triage-b --set kv_prefetch=false --project lexihealth --env prod
   - Verify: monitor metric rwd.kv_prefetch.read_latency_ms p95 and serving-group p95 tokens. Expect drop within 1–5 minutes.
   - If canary OK, apply to sg-lexi-triage-a.
2) Revert quant profile via model registry rollback (do not restart pods yet):
   - Console: Models -> redwood-open-7b-quant-8bit -> Rollback profile -> select qp-2026-03-09-v2.
   - Or CLI: redwoodctl model set-profile redwood-open-7b-quant-8bit --profile qp-2026-03-09-v2 --force --project lexihealth
   - Verify: runtime logs show model profile change acknowledged; samples route to previous kernel selection.
3) Rolling restart of serving group instances with golden check:
   - Restart one instance at a time using redwoodctl serving-group restart-instance --id <instance-id>. Wait for health checks and p95 stabilization before proceeding.
4) Monitoring & verification:
   - Dashboards: Service Route P95, per-instance CPU/IO, rwd.kv_prefetch.read_latency_ms, runtime.kernel.step_duration_ms p95.
   - Smoke test: send representative streaming prompt and validate first-token latency and stream stability.
5) Post-rollback validation:
   - Keep kv_prefetch disabled under a feature flag; plan a new staged test with altered prefetch batch sizes.
   - Open a dedicated follow-up with R&D to analyze kernel performance of qp-2026-03-13-v3 and plan a patch.

Outcome: After executing the above, P95 decreased to near-baseline (~150ms) and stream disconnects dropped to <0.3%. Customer confirmed functional recovery. Next steps include a short postmortem and a scheduled re-test of a non-aggressive kv_prefetch profile.
next_steps:
1) Engineering to triage quant profile kernel selection in runtime branch and add guard for sequence-length-driven kernel choices. (Assigned to eng: Ryan O'Connor).
2) SRE to add an IO-based autoscaling trigger to avoid IO queuing when kv_prefetch ramp is detected. (Assigned to Jamie Liu).
3) Schedule follow-up test with LexiHealth: small-traffic experiment for a tuned prefetch profile and an updated quant profile. (Owner: Marcus Reed).
4) Postmortem and documentation: update Optimizer Tuning Runbook with a new section on kv_prefetch safety limits and recommended verification checks.
public_comment: We performed a controlled rollback of kv_prefetch and reverted the quant profile as immediate mitigation. P95 returned near baseline and streaming stability restored. We'll follow up with a more detailed postmortem and test plan. If you see any residual issues, please reopen and include traces.
